title: Rishabh Instruments Ltd - 543977 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Rishabh Instruments FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 161% to INR1,264 mn (16.3% margin); 20% dividend declared and FY27 EEI growth guided at 20-25%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 7.6% to INR7,751 mn in FY26 and 9.3% to INR2,049 mn in Q4, while consolidated EBITDA more than doubled to INR1,264 mn and PAT rose 292% to INR823 mn. Standalone gross margin expanded to 54% from 48.6%, driven by product mix and sourcing. Lumel Alucast (HPDC) turned adjusted EBITDA positive at INR33 mn from a loss of INR150 mn, but its revenue fell 9.6% as loss-making contracts were exited. Management declared a 20% dividend (INR2 per INR10 share) and reported net cash of INR1,276 mn.

segments.name: Standalone Rishabh Instruments
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR788 mn (+15.2% YoY) with EBITDA INR161 mn (20.4% margin); FY26 PAT INR417 mn (+78.2%). US business grew about 50% to roughly USD3 mn, with a 40-50% growth target for FY27.

segments.name: Lumel SA (Poland, electronics)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR585 mn (+35.9% YoY) with adjusted EBITDA INR167 mn (28.6% margin); FY26 PAT INR419 mn (+19.5%). A new SMT line was commissioned, 40% funded by EU funds.

segments.name: Lumel Alucast (HPDC, Poland)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR575 mn (-22.8% YoY) with Q4 PAT loss of INR58 mn; FY26 PAT loss INR41 mn vs INR252 mn in FY25. Management targets no losses in FY27 and double-digit margins in FY28.

segments.name: Smaller entities (Shanghai V&A, Sifam Tinsley US and UK)
segments.commentary: Growth of 53% (US), 25% (UK) and 23% (China) on top line; together they are 13% of the EEI business and all three are EBITDA positive.

segments.name: Solar inverters (within EEI)
segments.commentary: Single-phase iUNO launched in H2 FY25 and now operationally profitable; FY27 target about INR24-25 crore, roughly double FY26.

guidance_outlook: EEI segment FY27 top-line growth guided at 20-25% (around 20-22% in the blended view), with EBITDA margin guided at 20-22%; management said margin could be higher.
Solar inverter sales target about INR24-25 crore in FY27; the new building can scale to about INR100 crore with incremental capex.
US business targeted at 40-50% growth in FY27 with a longer-term aim of about INR100 crore in 3-4 years.
Lumel Alucast FY27 revenue expected to be flat to slightly down, roughly INR180 crore in euro terms, with no losses; double-digit margin expected in FY28.
Asked about FY28 (March 2028), management said INR1,000 crore revenue may be close but not guaranteed, with EBITDA around INR200 crore if guidelines hold; for FY27 it cited INR150-160 crore EBITDA.
capex_capacity: Nashik expansion capex complete; two manufacturing facilities almost ready and under commissioning, expected to effectively double production capacity. Commissioning expected by June-July 2026.
Current transformer capacity being expanded from 6,000 to 10,000 units per day with additional lines, equipment and manpower.
Lumel SA commissioned an advanced SMT electronics assembly line in FY26, 40% funded by EU funds.
New building: one full floor dedicated to solar manufacturing, with assembly lines added as volume grows.
Medium-voltage CTs, PTs and VTs: 4-5 new products expected by end FY27, with sales from FY28; no plans for high-voltage products.
demand_pricing: Management expects Europe to be subdued, with US, Southeast Asia and Africa seeing rising power and automation investment.
Solar: Chinese SKD-based competitors are cheaper; management says about half of the product range is now cost-competitive. Europe solar is declining, so Middle East is the preferred next market.
Alucast: qualification cycles are long (volume arrives about one year after order booking); European HPDC competitors are closing and some business is shifting to India and China.
Pricing: management said it passes on material and cost increases in EEI because it owns its brands and prices.
Data centre and sectoral marketing (Sify repeat projects, UK and Ireland): the company is bundling products with software and hiring specification specialists.

qa_highlights.question: What growth and margin should be expected for the EEI business in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 20-25% top-line growth (about 20-22% blended) and 20-22% EBITDA margin; Rishabh and Lumel are each expected to grow about 20%, with smaller entities around 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Alucast's FY27 margin guidance unchanged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 is a transition year with no losses and no big margin targets; double-digit margin is expected in FY28, not FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will Alucast be demerged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no decision has been taken; a demerger is a possibility, but nothing is concrete and the company will inform the market at the right time.

qa_highlights.question: Is solar inverter cost-competitive with Chinese products, and what is the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is close but not yet fully competitive, with about half of the range competitive. FY27 target is INR24-25 crore, with OEM supply to assemblers and own-brand sales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US revenue and the long-term target?
qa_highlights.answer: US revenue reached about USD3 mn in FY26 (from USD2 mn), with 40-50% growth planned for FY27 and about INR100 crore targeted in 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company cross INR1,000 crore revenue and INR200 crore EBITDA by March 2028?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this is possible if guidelines hold but would not commit; the EEI business at INR560 crore growing 20% would reach about INR670 crore, while Alucast stays flat.

risks_watch: Alucast volume recovery: FY27 revenue could fall below INR200 crore (about INR180 crore in euro terms); breakeven depends on winning new projects and their qualification timelines.
Solar inverter profitability: management said margins are 15-20% gross, and cost competitiveness vs Chinese imports is incomplete.
Geopolitical and energy risk: management flagged West Asia war, oil shortages and tariffs as risks to FY27 guidance; rupee depreciation affects euro-based Lumel and Alucast figures.
Timing of the Nashik capacity commissioning (June-July 2026) and the medium-voltage product launches expected by end FY27.
Dividend sustainability: 20% dividend (INR2 per INR10 share) declared; an analyst asked about future payouts of 20% or more.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and the FY27 EEI guidance, but deliberately conservative. Management repeatedly stressed the 20-22% margin floor and was candid that Alucast FY27 is a no-loss transition with no growth. It was evasive on the Alucast demerger and on the 1,000 crore revenue question.

growth.why: Management guides EEI top-line growth of 20-25% for FY27 (blended ~20-22%) and Lumel Alucast flat to slightly down with no losses; Nashik capacity roughly doubling (commissioning June-July 2026) and CT capacity rising from 6,000 to 10,000 units/day support the EEI guide, though the brief gives no order-book figures for it.
